program.name: Tanner Pro Training
program.description: A 5 session progression built on Tanner Tomassi's coaching philosophy: efficient mechanics, real game decision making, and relentless kitchen line control. Players move from dink fundamentals to hands battles, footwork patterns, and live ball pressure training.

routines.name: Session 1 - Dink Foundation
routines.description: Build the push, not hit, dink mechanic and learn to control the kitchen line before adding any speed or pressure.

exercises.title: Push Dink Wall Drill
exercises.goal_text: 20 consecutive dinks with a closed paddle face, no pop ups
exercises.instructions:
Stand at the kitchen line facing a partner or wall.
Keep your wrist locked and imagine pushing through two stacked balls on your paddle.
Reach toward your target with a closed paddle face on contact.
Extend out in front, do not flick at the ball.
Count consecutive dinks that land in the kitchen without bouncing high.
tips: Think push, not hit, like pushing two stacked balls forward
Closed paddle face keeps the ball low and in the kitchen
Let the ball hit you, do not reach early

exercises.title: Straight Ahead Dink Game with Speedups
exercises.goal_text: Sustain a controlled cross court dink rally and execute 5 clean speedups when the ball pops up
exercises.instructions:
Line up directly across from your partner at the kitchen line.
Exchange controlled dinks down the line, staying patient.
Whenever the ball sits up or floats, accelerate the pace with a speedup.
Reset to dinking immediately after the speedup is returned.
Repeat for 10 minutes, tracking how many clean speedups you land.
tips: This is how you take control of the kitchen line
Only speed up balls that are above net height
Stay low and lean into the kitchen after you dink

exercises.title: Net Clip Discipline Drill
exercises.goal_text: Recognize 10 net clipped balls in a row and correctly choose not to speed them up
exercises.instructions:
Play a normal dink rally with a partner.
When a ball clips the top of the net, immediately reset to a soft dink instead of attacking it.
A net clipped ball loses pace and is a low value target, do not get baited into a low percentage speedup.
Have your partner track how many times you correctly held back versus incorrectly attacked.
tips: A net clipped ball has lost most of its momentum
Speeding up a net ball is a common amateur mistake
Patience here sets up your next real opportunity

exercises.title: Closed Paddle Face Target Reach
exercises.goal_text: Land 15 of 20 dinks inside a towel placed in the kitchen near the sideline
exercises.instructions:
Place a towel or target near the sideline corner of the kitchen.
Dink toward the target using a closed paddle face and a forward reach.
Finish your reach out in front of your body, not across it.
Count how many dinks land on or inside the target out of 20 attempts.
tips: An open paddle face sends the ball up, keep it closed
Finishing out in front keeps the shot low and accurate
Accuracy first, pace second

exercises.title: Let It Hit You Mental Rep
exercises.goal_text: Complete 10 dinks where you consciously delay contact and let the ball travel to you
exercises.instructions:
Start a slow dink rally with a partner.
Focus only on patience, resist the urge to reach at the ball early.
Let the ball come all the way to your paddle before initiating the push.
Call out 'late' on any rep where you caught yourself reaching early, and reset the count.
tips: This is a mental game shift as much as a mechanical one
Reaching early causes most pop up dinks
Stay relaxed, the ball will arrive

routines.name: Session 2 - Drive or Drop Decision Making
routines.description: Develop pickleball IQ by learning the exact scenarios where you should drive the third shot versus drop it, based on Tanner's return read system.

exercises.title: Short and High Return Drive Drill
exercises.goal_text: Drive 8 of 10 short, high returns with pace into the opponent's body or feet
exercises.instructions:
Have a feeder hit returns that bounce short and high in the court.
Recognize this as a drive opportunity, the ball sits up and invites pace.
Step in and drive the ball flat and low, targeting the body or feet of the opponent at the kitchen line.
Track makes versus misses out of 10 reps.
tips: Short and high bounces are a green light to apply pressure
Target the body or feet, not open space
Drive flat, do not loop it

exercises.title: Off Balance Deep Return Drive
exercises.goal_text: Successfully drive 8 of 10 deep aggressive returns hit while off your back foot
exercises.instructions:
Have a feeder hit deep, aggressive returns that push you off your back foot.
Instead of trying to drop from an unstable position, drive the ball back with pace.
The goal is to get an easier next ball to drop, not to win the point outright.
Reset to neutral positioning after each drive.
tips: When you are off balance and deep, drive instead of dropping
The drive buys you time and an easier follow up shot
Recover toward center immediately after contact

exercises.title: Shallow Low Return Drop Drill
exercises.goal_text: Land 8 of 10 third shot drops in the kitchen off a shallow, low feed
exercises.instructions:
Have a feeder hit returns that bounce shallow in the court but stay low.
Recognize that a low ball does not give you the height to drive safely.
Hit a soft third shot drop that lands in the kitchen.
Focus on arc and touch rather than pace.
tips: Low shallow balls are a drop situation, not a drive situation
Prioritize arc and soft hands over power
Land it in the kitchen to neutralize the point

exercises.title: Deep Soft Return Drop Drill
exercises.goal_text: Land 8 of 10 drops off a deep but soft return near the baseline
exercises.instructions:
Have a feeder hit returns that land deep near the baseline but with soft pace.
Recognize this as a drop scenario since the ball lacks the pace to drive effectively.
Use a longer, smoother stroke to drop the ball into the kitchen from deep court.
Track consistency across 10 reps.
tips: Deep and soft means drop, deep and hard usually means drive
Give yourself more swing path from deeper court position
Soft hands win this rep

exercises.title: Live Read and React Decision Drill
exercises.goal_text: Correctly identify drive versus drop and execute it on 7 of 10 randomized live feeds
exercises.instructions:
Have a feeder randomly mix all four return types from this session, short and high, deep and aggressive, shallow and low, deep and soft.
React in real time, calling out drive or drop before contact, then execute the correct shot.
A feeder or coach scores each rep as a correct or incorrect decision plus a make or miss.
This simulates real match decision making under time pressure.
tips: This is the IQ rep, decision speed matters as much as execution
When in doubt, default to the drop, it is the lower risk shot
Call your decision out loud before contact to build the habit

routines.name: Session 3 - Hands Battles and Fast Exchanges
routines.description: Sharpen reaction speed and hand quickness at the kitchen line through controlled hands battles, Tanner's favorite drill for developing fast hands and ball reading.

exercises.title: Soft Dead Dink Trigger Drill
exercises.goal_text: Initiate 10 clean hands battles by setting up with a dead dink before the exchange
exercises.instructions:
Start at the kitchen line with a partner, exchanging normal dinks.
On your turn, hit a soft, dead dink with very little pace.
This is the trigger, your partner will then accelerate the pace to start the hands battle.
Focus only on setting up the trigger cleanly for this rep.
tips: The dead dink is intentionally low pace to invite an attack
This is how Tanner starts every hands battle rep
Stay ready immediately after you hit the dead dink

exercises.title: Hands Battle Reaction Drill
exercises.goal_text: Win or neutrally survive 6 of 10 hands battle exchanges
exercises.instructions:
After the dead dink trigger, your partner accelerates and the hands battle begins.
Block and counter punch volleys at the kitchen line, prioritizing soft hands over swinging.
Keep your paddle up and out in front, reacting rather than initiating big swings.
Track how many exchanges you win outright or end in a neutral reset, not a clean loss.
tips: This is how you develop fast hands and good ball reading
Block first, counter second, do not try to overpower every ball
Keep your paddle out in front, never let it drop

exercises.title: Crosscourt Wide to Middle Coverage
exercises.goal_text: Successfully return 8 of 10 reps moving from a wide dink to covering the middle
exercises.instructions:
Stand crosscourt from your partner at the kitchen line.
Partner starts with a wide dink pulling you out to the sideline.
Return the wide dink, then immediately shuffle step back toward center.
Partner then moves the next ball to the middle, you must cover it without crossing your feet.
tips: Get into the habit of recovering to the middle after being pulled wide
Use shuffle steps, do not cross your feet at the net
This pattern shows up constantly in doubles play

exercises.title: Banger Crash Defense Drill
exercises.goal_text: Successfully neutralize 6 of 10 hard driven balls from a partner crashing the net
exercises.instructions:
Position yourself at the kitchen line while your partner stands just inside the baseline.
Partner feeds themselves a ball and drives it hard while crashing forward to the net.
Your job is to handle the pace and chaos, blocking the drive into a controllable reset.
Do not try to speed up the incoming drive, absorb the pace and reset to a dink.
tips: This simulates dealing with aggressive bangers crashing the net
Absorb pace with soft hands, do not match power with power
A clean reset is a win against an attacking drive

exercises.title: Lob Recovery and Reset Drill
exercises.goal_text: Recover and reset 7 of 10 overhead lobs hit to put you on defense
exercises.instructions:
Partner hits a lob over your head while you are at the kitchen line.
Turn and track the ball, moving back with crossover steps rather than backpedaling flat footed.
Hit the ball back deep or as a controlled reset, then move back up to the kitchen line.
Track how many reps you recover from cleanly without giving up an easy put away.
tips: Turn your hips and track the ball over your shoulder, do not backpedal
Recovering forward after the lob is just as important as the defense itself
Aim deep to buy yourself time to get back to the line

routines.name: Session 4 - Flicks, Slices, and Tricky Returns
routines.description: Tackle the shots players avoid most: backhand flicks and slice returns, broken down into simple footwork and timing cues.

exercises.title: Sideways Stance Backhand Flick Drill
exercises.goal_text: Execute 8 of 10 backhand flicks with proper sideways stance and full body rotation
exercises.instructions:
Start in a square stance facing the net at the kitchen line.
As the ball approaches on your backhand side, turn your feet sideways before contact.
Rotate through your obliques and core, not just your arm, to generate pace.
Flick the ball flat and aggressive at your target, tracking clean makes out of 10.
tips: Turning sideways lets your whole body engage, not just your arm
A square stance flick will feel weak and awkward
This is simpler than it looks once the footwork is right

exercises.title: Slice Return Timing Drill
exercises.goal_text: Cleanly handle 8 of 10 slice serves or returns without mistiming contact
exercises.instructions:
Have a feeder hit slice serves or slice returns with sidespin.
Watch the spin direction before committing to your paddle angle.
Adjust your paddle face slightly against the spin direction to control the ball.
Focus on a clean, controlled contact rather than trying to attack the slice.
tips: Slices are designed to mess with your timing, stay patient
Read the spin early, adjust your paddle angle accordingly
Control first, then look to attack on the next ball

exercises.title: Good Dink to Pop Up Anticipation Drill
exercises.goal_text: Correctly anticipate and attack 7 of 10 pop ups generated by your own aggressive dink
exercises.instructions:
Hit an aggressive, pressuring dink that is likely to generate a pop up.
Immediately set your paddle head down and elbow up, leaning in to anticipate the pop up.
When the pop up comes, attack it in one fluid motion without delay.
Avoid the common mistake of standing flat footed and reaching late.
tips: Paddle head down, elbow up, lean in after a good aggressive dink
Anticipate the pop up instead of reacting late to it
One fluid motion beats a standing reach every time

exercises.title: Drop Volley Discipline Drill
exercises.goal_text: Correctly choose to apply pressure instead of attempting a low value drop volley on 9 of 10 reps
exercises.instructions:
Have a feeder hit a third shot drop to you at the kitchen line while standing at the baseline.
Resist the urge to attempt a drop volley back into the kitchen.
Instead, hit a firm, controlled shot to keep your opponent back.
Only attempt the drop volley if the feed is clearly off balance and weak.
tips: A mistimed drop volley hands your opponent a free trip to the net
Apply pressure and keep them back unless the ball is clearly weak
This decision alone separates intermediate players from advanced ones

exercises.title: Mixed Shot IQ Circuit
exercises.goal_text: Score 30 of 40 total reps correctly across flicks, slices, anticipation, and drop volley decisions
exercises.instructions:
Run 10 reps each of the backhand flick, slice return, pop up anticipation, and drop volley discipline drills back to back.
A coach or partner tracks correct decisions and clean execution across all 40 reps.
This circuit combines mechanics and decision making under light fatigue.
Use this as a checkpoint before moving into full pressure training.
tips: This circuit is a checkpoint, not a new skill
Fatigue exposes mechanical breakdowns, stay disciplined
Quality of decision matters as much as clean contact

routines.name: Session 5 - Live Pressure and Mental Game
routines.description: Apply everything under match like pressure, including Tanner's mindset framework for handling nerves and tournament situations.

exercises.title: Hold to Disguise Speedup Drill
exercises.goal_text: Disguise 7 of 10 speedups by holding the shot before attacking
exercises.instructions:
Engage in a dink rally with a partner.
When you get a speedup opportunity, briefly hold the shot rather than attacking immediately.
The hold creates hesitation in your opponent since they cannot predict the direction.
After the hold, attack decisively at your chosen target.
tips: If you hold, your opponent cannot guess where the speedup is going
The hold is a timing weapon, not a hesitation mistake
Commit fully once you decide to attack

exercises.title: Full Point Live Play from Serve
exercises.goal_text: Win or competitively contest 6 of 10 full points started from a live serve
exercises.instructions:
Play out full points starting from an actual serve and return.
Apply the drive versus drop decision rules from Session 2 on your third shot.
Use the hands battle and dink control skills once you reach the kitchen line.
Track points won or lost out of 10 full point reps.
tips: This is where all prior sessions come together
Stick to your decision rules even under live pressure
Reset your mindset after every point, win or lose

exercises.title: Pressure Release Mindset Rep
exercises.goal_text: Complete 5 pressure points while verbally practicing the weight transfer mindset cue
exercises.instructions:
Play single pressure points, such as serving at match point down.
Before each point, say out loud the cue, the pressure is on my opponent, not on me.
Focus on competing freely rather than playing not to lose.
Debrief after each point on whether you felt tight or free.
tips: Take the weight off your shoulders and put it on your opponent
Nervous opponents make mistakes, let the pressure work for you
This mental rep matters most in tournament settings

exercises.title: First to the Net Wins Doubles Rule
exercises.goal_text: Apply the simple net rule across 8 of 10 doubles points by reaching the kitchen line first
exercises.instructions:
Play doubles points with a partner against another team.
Agree before each point that whoever can safely get to the kitchen line first should do so.
Focus on transitioning quickly and safely rather than rushing recklessly.
Track how many points your team established net position first.
tips: Setting this rule with your partner keeps you both grounded
Nervous opponents at the net often make the first mistake
Transition with split steps, not a flat out sprint

exercises.title: Tanner Pro Training Final Assessment
exercises.goal_text: Score 35 of 50 total reps across a mixed live play checkpoint combining all five sessions
exercises.instructions:
Run a combined assessment covering dink control, drive or drop decisions, hands battles, flicks and slices, and live point play.
A coach scores execution and decision making across 50 total reps.
Use the results to identify which session the player should revisit.
This assessment marks the completion of the Tanner Pro Training program.
tips: This is a comprehensive checkpoint, not a new skill to learn
Use the result to plan the player's next training block
Celebrate progress, then set the next goal
